heard: A massive star is spinning so fast it flings off its surface. Located 550 light years away, gamma cassiope marks the central point of the celestial W in Cassiopeia. Rotating at roughly 450 kilometers per second, this bulged star is on the brink of structural breakup. Radiating 19,000 times more energy than the sun, its intense radiation is actively vaporizing nearby nebulae. For five decades, astronomers faced an unsolved puzzle. The star blazed with X-rays reaching 150 million degrees. In 2026, the XRISM space telescope unmasked the culprit by tracking Doppler shifts in the hot plasma. The radiation doesn't come from the giant, but from a hidden, Earth-sized white dwarf companion. Every 203 days, this dense corpse feeds on material shed by an unraveling giant.
